and.name: Model_Federation
and.description: Represents the NAOMI platform approach for multi-modeling, enabling multiple models developed in different DSMLs to work together by analyzing dependencies and coordinating change propagation, extended with MDE-based interoperability concepts, security-oriented evolution, quality assessment integration, architecture recovery mechanisms, view-based consistency preservation approaches like Vitruvius, Multi-Paradigm Modelling (MPM) capabilities via the Modelverse, reactive links for fine-grained change propagation, Linked Data approaches for tool interoperability, the SeMMA architecture for semantic multi-modeling, and the integration of multiple non-functional properties analysis.

and.name: Structural
and.description: Covers the artefacts, links, and structural features of Model Federation, including model composition, graph structure, formalism, domain, and technological context.

and.name: Repository_Artifacts
and.description: Entities stored in the Multi-Model Repository that define the multi-model, including models, registries, interfaces, constraints, federation-specific structures, recovered architectural representations, V-SUM artifacts, FTG+PM models, reactive links, Linked Data resources, SeMMA correspondence models, and NFP analysis models.

and.name: Models
and.description: The core entities representing mappings written in specific languages over sets of inputs and outputs.

or.name: Model_Types
or.description: Classification of models into Specification and Analytical groups, which are not necessarily exclusive.

feature.name: Specification_Models
feature.description: Models that help define the system being modeled, such as UML class hierarchies or state diagrams. Trace: [Article_1.pdf §3.1 NAOMI Multi-model Repository]

feature.name: Analytical_Models
feature.description: Models that analyze aspects of the defined system, such as evaluating safety parameters using RT-Maude. Trace: [Article_1.pdf §3.1 NAOMI Multi-model Repository]

feature.name: Model_Registry
feature.description: A simple list used to determine membership in the multi-model by enumerating the models involved. Trace: [Article_1.pdf §3.1 NAOMI Multi-model Repository]

feature.name: Model_Attributes
feature.description: Inputs and outputs associated with models, used for data exchange and synchronization. Trace: [Article_1.pdf §3.1 NAOMI Multi-model Repository]

feature.name: Model_Interfaces
feature.description: The tuple representation of a model including its language, inputs, and outputs, exposed to the system. Trace: [Article_1.pdf §3.1 NAOMI Multi-model Repository]

feature.name: Attribute_Constraints
feature.description: Triggers on attribute values that notify models if an input violates a constraint or ensure output validity. Trace: [Article_1.pdf §3.1 NAOMI Multi-model Repository]

feature.name: Notifications
feature.description: Messages sent to models to inform them of interesting events, such as constraint violations. Trace: [Article_1.pdf §3.1 NAOMI Multi-model Repository]

feature.name: Model_Editing_Tools
feature.description: The tools used to create and modify the models, which are stored as artifacts in the repository. Trace: [Article_1.pdf §3.1 NAOMI Multi-model Repository]

feature.name: Ontology
feature.description: A formal knowledge foundation for simulation models using ontology techniques to support semantic description and inference. Trace: [Article_10.pdf::chunk::21; Article_10.pdf::chunk::34]

feature.name: Metamodel
feature.description: Defines the abstract syntax and static semantics of Domain Specific Modeling Languages (DSML), such as the SMDL in SMP2. Trace: [Article_10.pdf::chunk::35]

feature.name: Virtual_Model
feature.description: A model in the Federation Model Language (FML) that serves as an interaction model capturing dependencies between model elements in different models. Trace: [Article_11.pdf::chunk::35]

feature.name: Flexo_Concepts
feature.description: Metaclasses in the interaction model used to establish links between elements in participating models, such as linking a Pool element to an Artifact element. Trace: [Article_11.pdf::chunk::36]

feature.name: Model_Slots
feature.description: Technological connectors in OpenFlexo used to enable concepts to access information on external models not directly defined in FML. Trace: [Article_11.pdf::chunk::36]

feature.name: Security_Rules
feature.description: Rules defined to describe consistency in the form of security requirements, manually attached to links to be (re)evaluated upon changes to detect violations. Trace: [Article_11.pdf::chunk::25; Article_11.pdf::chunk::38]

feature.name: Viewpoint_Contract
feature.description: A technique evolved from design contracts that defines key vocabulary, assumptions, and obligations for communication among stakeholders across different viewpoints. Trace: [Article_3.pdf::chunk::11; Article_3.pdf::chunk::129]

feature.name: Dependency_Model
feature.description: A model used to explicitly codify relations between product properties captured by models related to different viewpoints, often used to manage dependencies. Trace: [Article_3.pdf::chunk::129; Article_3.pdf::chunk::137]

and.name: Multimodel_Structure
and.description: Defines the structural components of a multimodel, which is a set of interrelated models representing different viewpoints of a system.

feature.name: Viewpoint
feature.description: An abstraction that yields the specification of the whole system restricted to a particular set of concerns, created with a specific purpose in mind. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::5; Article_12.pdf::chunk::11]

feature.name: Viewpoint_Model
feature.description: A model of the system from a specific viewpoint, containing only the objects visible from that viewpoint. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::5; Article_12.pdf::chunk::11]

feature.name: Multimodel_Entity
feature.description: Additional entities in a multimodel that extend entities on different viewpoint models to hold inter-viewpoint relationships. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::6; Article_12.pdf::chunk::13]

feature.name: Multimodel_Relationship
feature.description: Relationships defined among elements on different viewpoints, involving two multimodel entities that extend model entities. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::6; Article_12.pdf::chunk::13]

feature.name: Multimodel_Attributes
feature.description: Attributes used for storing multimodel information on MultimodelEntity or MultimodelRelationship elements. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::6; Article_12.pdf::chunk::13]

and.name: Viewpoint_Types
and.description: Specific types of viewpoints identified in the multimodel definition process, such as those for variability, quality, functionality, and transformations.

feature.name: Variability_Viewpoint
feature.description: A viewpoint introduced to represent variability management, crucial in domains like software product lines. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::20]

feature.name: Quality_Viewpoint
feature.description: A viewpoint introduced for the explicit representation of quality information and product quality improvement. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::20]

feature.name: Functional_Viewpoint
feature.description: A viewpoint used to represent the structure and components that a system comprises, often using an Architectural Description Language. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::20]

feature.name: Transformation_Viewpoint
feature.description: A viewpoint used to model the different transformation processes that occur during the development process. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::20]

or.name: Relationship_Types
or.description: The different semantics that inter-viewpoint relationships can have, such as implication, exclusion, or impact.

feature.name: Implication_Relationship
feature.description: A relationship where a model element A in one viewpoint implies an element B in another viewpoint. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::28]

feature.name: Co-Implication_Relationship
feature.description: A relationship where a model element A implies an element B and vice versa. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::28]

feature.name: Exclusion_Relationship
feature.description: A relationship where a model element A excludes an element B in another viewpoint. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::28]

feature.name: Decomposition_Relationship
feature.description: A relationship where a model element A is decomposed into elements in other viewpoints. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::28]

feature.name: Representation_Relationship
feature.description: A relationship where a model element A is represented by a set of elements in another viewpoint. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::29]

feature.name: Impact_Relationship
feature.description: A relationship where a model element A impacts an element B in another viewpoint, often used for quality attributes. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::30]

feature.name: Constraint_Relationship
feature.description: Complex relationships at the multimodel level, similar to OCL restrictions, used to express constraints. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::31]

and.name: Megamodel
and.description: A model representing the structure of an MDE project, including typed nodes and relationships among artifacts like metamodels, models, and transformations, used for architecture recovery.

and.name: Virtual_Artifact
and.description: Artifacts computed to facilitate relationship recovery, such as Typing Requirements Models (TRM) or Domain Requirements Models (DRM), which may not exist physically in the project.

feature.name: Typing_Requirements_Model
feature.description: A Typing Requirements Model (TRM) describing the requirements a transformation needs from source and target metamodels for syntactically correct typing. Trace: [Article_14.pdf::chunk::102]

feature.name: Domain_Requirements_Model
feature.description: A Domain Requirements Model (DRM) generated from a TRM, describing requirements for source and target metamodels. Trace: [Article_14.pdf::chunk::103]

feature.name: Auxiliary_Node
feature.description: Nodes added to the graph during the recovery process to represent virtual artifacts or temporary links, such as DRMs. Trace: [Article_14.pdf::chunk::104]

and.name: V-SUM_Artifacts
and.description: Artifacts specific to the Vitruvius approach for view-based consistency, including the V-SUM metamodel, correspondence models, and view type definitions.

feature.name: V-SUM_Metamodel
feature.description: A metamodel containing a set of metamodels, consistency preservation rules, and view types, defining the structure of a View-based System Under Modeling. Trace: [Article_2.pdf::chunk::104; Article_2.pdf::chunk::108]

feature.name: Correspondence_Model
feature.description: A trace model used to identify which elements are related to each other in terms of fulfilling a consistency rule, storing explicit relations between elements. Trace: [Article_2.pdf::chunk::104; Article_2.pdf::chunk::117]

feature.name: View_Type
feature.description: A definition of a view with a projectional-complete scope, representing all elements in a metamodel or aggregating information from multiple models, often used to replace original metamodels. Trace: [Article_2.pdf::chunk::121; Article_2.pdf::chunk::124]

and.name: FTG_PM_Model
and.description: A model consisting of a Formalism Transformation Graph (FTG) and a Process Model (PM), used to provide an overview of formalisms, operations, and their execution order in Multi-Paradigm Modelling. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::15; Article_4.pdf §chunk::16]

feature.name: Formalism_Transformation_Graph
feature.description: The part of the FTG+PM model that presents all used formalisms as nodes and their relations (operations) as links. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::15; Article_4.pdf §chunk::16]

feature.name: Process_Model
feature.description: The part of the FTG+PM model that mandates the order of operations to execute and specifies the models (data) they operate on. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::15; Article_4.pdf §chunk::16]

feature.name: Reactive_Link
feature.description: Links that establish connections between related properties in different artifacts to automatically propagate fine-grained changes and prevent inconsistencies. Trace: [Article_5.pdf::chunk::13; Article_5.pdf::chunk::36]

and.name: Link_Operators
and.description: Operators used to define the behavior of a reactive link, such as assignment for propagation or equality for consistency checking.

feature.name: Assignment_Operator
feature.description: An operator used to define the propagation direction of a reactive link, typically indicating that a value is copied from source to target. Trace: [Article_5.pdf::chunk::101]

feature.name: Equality_Operator
feature.description: An operator used to check if two property values are equal, often used in the reverse direction of a link to detect inconsistencies. Trace: [Article_5.pdf::chunk::101]

feature.name: DesignSpace_Meta-Metamodel
feature.description: A DesignSpace-specific meta-metamodel used to store engineering data in a uniform representation, combining model and metamodel information. Trace: [Article_5.pdf::chunk::132; Article_5.pdf::chunk::133]

and.name: DesignSpace_Representation
and.description: The uniform data structure in DesignSpace consisting of InstanceTypes, PropertyTypes, and Instances to represent tool artifacts.

feature.name: InstanceTypes
feature.description: Structures in DesignSpace that describe the type of a model element, corresponding to the metamodel of the domain. Trace: [Article_5.pdf::chunk::134]

feature.name: PropertyTypes
feature.description: Definitions in DesignSpace that describe the properties of an InstanceType, including generic types or references to custom types. Trace: [Article_5.pdf::chunk::135]

feature.name: Instances
feature.description: Artifacts in DesignSpace that represent specific model elements, storing data in properties defined by their InstanceType. Trace: [Article_5.pdf::chunk::135]

and.name: Linked_Data_Resources
and.description: Artifacts defined within a Linked Data approach to tool interoperability, representing resources, their properties, and constraints according to RDF and OSLC standards.

feature.name: Resource_Type
feature.description: Entities defined in the F-IDE, represented as ellipses in the domain specification view, which correspond to resources in the RDF graph data model. Trace: [Article_6.pdf::chunk::32; Article_6.pdf::chunk::36]

feature.name: Resource_Property
feature.description: First-class elements defining the allowed and required properties of a resource type, including cardinality, optionality, and value-type. Trace: [Article_6.pdf::chunk::28; Article_6.pdf::chunk::47]

feature.name: Literal_Property
feature.description: A resource property whose value-type is a predefined literal type such as string or integer. Trace: [Article_6.pdf::chunk::34]

feature.name: Reference_Property
feature.description: A resource property whose value-type is set to resource or local resource, used to define relationships between resources. Trace: [Article_6.pdf::chunk::34]

feature.name: Local_Resource
feature.description: A resource that exists only within the context of a parent resource and does not have its own URI. Trace: [Article_6.pdf::chunk::48]

and.name: NFP_Analysis_Models
and.description: Models used to verify non-functional properties such as performance, reliability, or security, often derived from software models. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::2; Article_9.pdf::chunk::19]

feature.name: Queueing_Networks
feature.description: Performance models capturing contention for resources, often used for analytical solutions. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::19; Article_9.pdf::chunk::35]

feature.name: Stochastic_Petri_Nets
feature.description: Flow models representing concurrency, solved via Markov chain-based solutions. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::19; Article_9.pdf::chunk::37]

feature.name: Stochastic_Process_Algebra
feature.description: Compositional approach breaking systems into subsystems, based on languages like PEPA. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::19; Article_9.pdf::chunk::25]

feature.name: Markov_Chains
feature.description: Stochastic models with discrete state space used as underlying solutions for other analytical models. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::19; Article_9.pdf::chunk::21]

feature.name: Fault_Trees
feature.description: Models used for dependability analysis and safety-critical systems. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::19; Article_9.pdf::chunk::32]

feature.name: Probabilistic_Time_Automata
feature.description: Formalisms used for NFP analysis. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::19]

feature.name: Formal_Logic
feature.description: Formalisms used for NFP analysis, such as first-order logic in Alloy. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::19; Article_9.pdf::chunk::29]

feature.name: Layered_Queueing_Networks
feature.description: An extension of Queueing Networks used as a target model for performance analysis. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::24; Article_9.pdf::chunk::37]

feature.name: Bayesian_Belief_Network
feature.description: Models used for decision support under uncertainty to derive fitness scores for designs. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::35]

and.name: Modeling_Space_Modularity
and.description: Defines the dimensions of modularity in a multi-model system, separating structural placement of features from conceptual projections to manage complexity and coupling.

feature.name: Structural_Modularity
feature.description: Places all features, primarily serving for a common concern, in a single model (a module) to achieve structural modularization. Trace: [Article_8.pdf::chunk::11]

feature.name: Conceptual_Modularity
feature.description: Looks for the projections of secondary concerns of features in conceptual space and creates modules out of the overlapping or tightly coupled features from different models. Trace: [Article_8.pdf::chunk::11]

and.name: Modeling_Languages
and.description: Formalisms and languages selected to express the concepts associated with specific concerns in the multimodel.

and.name: Quality_Model_Language
and.description: Languages or models used to express quality concerns of an organization.

feature.name: SQuaRE
feature.description: Software product Quality Requirements and Evaluation standard used as a basis for quality models. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::17; Article_12.pdf::chunk::23]

feature.name: QUAMOCO
feature.description: A quality model approach used as a formalism for the quality viewpoint. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::17; Article_12.pdf::chunk::23]

and.name: Variability_Modeling_Language
and.description: Languages used to represent variability in a software product line.

feature.name: Cardinality_Based_Feature_Model
feature.description: A feature modeling language supporting cardinalities, selected for the variability viewpoint. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::17; Article_12.pdf::chunk::23]

and.name: Architectural_Description_Language
and.description: Languages used to describe the software architecture and its components in the functional viewpoint.

feature.name: AADL
feature.description: Architecture Analysis and Design Language, an ADL used to specify the functional viewpoint. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::17; Article_12.pdf::chunk::23]

feature.name: SYSML
feature.description: Systems Modeling Language, an ADL option for describing software architecture. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::17; Article_12.pdf::chunk::23]

feature.name: UML
feature.description: Unified Modeling Language, an ADL option for describing software architecture. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::17; Article_12.pdf::chunk::23]

feature.name: EAST-ADL
feature.description: Electronic Architecture and Software Technology - Architecture Description Language, an ADL used in automotive domains. Trace: [Article_12.pdf::chunk::17; Article_12.pdf::chunk::23]

feature.name: Palladio_Component_Model
feature.description: An architectural description language used for modeling software architectures to support quantitative performance, reliability, and cost prediction. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::34]

and.name: Metamodeling_Language
and.description: Languages used to define metamodels, which describe the abstract syntax of modeling languages.

feature.name: KM3
feature.description: Kernel MetaMetaModel, a DSL for describing metamodels with a specific textual notation to enhance agility and precision. Trace: [Article_14.pdf::chunk::109]

and.name: Model_to_Text_Language
and.description: Languages used to transform models into text artifacts, such as code or documentation.

feature.name: Acceleo
feature.description: An MDE tool implementing the MOFM2T standard for model-to-text transformation, used for code generation and visualization. Trace: [Article_14.pdf::chunk::113; Article_14.pdf::chunk::120]

and.name: Consistency_Languages
and.description: Languages used to define consistency preservation rules and transformations between models in a view-based development process.

feature.name: Reactions_Language
feature.description: An imperative language used for unidirectional specification of consistency preservation rules (CPRs), providing maximum expressiveness and declarative constructs for recurring actions. Trace: [Article_2.pdf::chunk::40; Article_2.pdf::chunk::139]

feature.name: Mappings_Language
feature.description: A highly declarative language used for bidirectional specification of consistency rules (CRs), which are transformed into imperative specifications of the Reactions language. Trace: [Article_2.pdf::chunk::40; Article_2.pdf::chunk::134]

and.name: Tool_Integration_Language
and.description: Languages for describing tool chains systematically, graphically and with well-defined semantics to support tool integration.

feature.name: TIL
feature.description: A domain specific modeling language (DSML) for describing tool chains systematically, graphically and with well-defined semantics. Trace: [Article_3.pdf::chunk::100]

and.name: TIL_Concepts
and.description: The abstract syntax concepts defined by the Tool Integration Language (TIL) to represent tool chain elements.

feature.name: ToolChain_Concept
feature.description: A container for all elements of a tool chain, which can be composed hierarchically. Trace: [Article_3.pdf::chunk::102]

feature.name: ToolAdapter_Concept
feature.description: Exposes functionality and data of an integrated tool, adapting between the tool's technical space and the integration space. Trace: [Article_3.pdf::chunk::102]

feature.name: ToolAdapterMetamodel_Concept
feature.description: Specifies the structure of data and signature of functionality exposed by a ToolAdapter. Trace: [Article_3.pdf::chunk::103]

feature.name: ControlChannel_Concept
feature.description: Describes concurrent control flow, specifying source/target components and services. Trace: [Article_3.pdf::chunk::104]

feature.name: Sequencer_Concept
feature.description: Allows for sequential control flow, executing a sequence of services in a defined order. Trace: [Article_3.pdf::chunk::105]

feature.name: User_Concept
feature.description: A representative for a real tool chain user, describing interactions and notifications. Trace: [Article_3.pdf::chunk::105]

feature.name: DataChannel_Concept
feature.description: Transfers data between ToolAdapters, potentially attaching model transformations to resolve heterogeneities. Trace: [Article_3.pdf::chunk::106]

feature.name: TraceChannel_Concept
feature.description: Describes the possibility to establish trace links between tool data at runtime. Trace: [Article_3.pdf::chunk::107]

feature.name: Repository_Concept
feature.description: A tool adapter providing storage and version management, e.g., for SVN. Trace: [Article_3.pdf::chunk::108]

and.name: Dependency_Modeling_Language
and.description: Languages used to explicitly codify relations between product properties captured by models related to different viewpoints.

feature.name: DML
feature.description: The language used to define dependency models, referenced by the DMLToolAdapter. Trace: [Article_3.pdf::chunk::139; Article_3.pdf::chunk::140]

and.name: Language_Engineering
and.description: The aspect of Multi-Paradigm Modelling (MPM) involving the creation and instantiation of new modelling languages (DSMLs) through meta-modelling to close the conceptual gap between problem and solution domains. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::24; Article_4.pdf §chunk::25]

feature.name: Meta_Circularity
feature.description: A property of the meta-hierarchy where the topmost language is an instance of itself, preventing infinite recursion in language definition. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::26]

and.name: Domain_Specific_Languages
and.description: Languages tailored to specific problem domains that decrease verbosity, increase conceptual clarity, and maximally constrain the modeller. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::25; Article_4.pdf §chunk::31]

feature.name: SCCD
feature.description: A modelling language combining Class Diagrams and Statecharts, created through language engineering. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::25]

feature.name: Plant_DSL
feature.description: A domain-specific language used to model the plant component of a power window system. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::33]

feature.name: Control_DSL
feature.description: A domain-specific language used to model the control logic of a power window system. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::33]

feature.name: Query_DSL
feature.description: A domain-specific language used to model safety queries for verification. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::33]

feature.name: Environment_DSL
feature.description: A domain-specific language used to model the environment interactions of a power window system. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::33]

feature.name: Architecture_DSL
feature.description: A domain-specific language used to model the architecture of the system. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::33]

feature.name: Petri_Nets
feature.description: A mathematical modelling language applicable to many systems, used in the example for reachability analysis and as a target for transformations. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::21; Article_4.pdf §chunk::38]

feature.name: RAMification
feature.description: A technique for explicit modelling of model transformations by Relaxing, Augmenting, and Modifying an existing language, allowing operations to be treated as models. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::41; Article_4.pdf §chunk::45]

feature.name: Action_Language
feature.description: An imperative language (e.g., EOL) used to define model operations, suitable for well-studied algorithms like reachability analysis. Trace: [Article_4.pdf §chunk::40; Article_4.pdf §chunk::50]

and.name: Linked_Data_Languages
and.description: Languages and standards used to define and constrain Linked Data resources for tool interoperability.

feature.name: RDF
feature.description: Resource Description Framework graph data model used as the basis for Linked Data resources. Trace: [Article_6.pdf::chunk::20]

feature.name: RDFS
feature.description: RDF Schema used for standard specifications in the domain view. Trace: [Article_6.pdf::chunk::33]

feature.name: FOAF
feature.description: Friend of a Friend standard specification supported in the domain view. Trace: [Article_6.pdf::chunk::33]

feature.name: Resource_Shapes_Language
feature.description: A mechanism to define constraints on RDF resources, specifying allowed properties, cardinality, and ranges. Trace: [Article_6.pdf::chunk::28]

and.name: NFP_Annotation_Language
and.description: Languages or profiles used to annotate software models with non-functional property information. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::26; Article_9.pdf::chunk::27]

feature.name: SPT_Profile
feature.description: UML Profile for Schedulability, Performance, and Time defined for UML 1.x. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::27]

feature.name: MARTE_Profile
feature.description: UML Profile for Modeling and Analysis of Real-Time and Embedded systems defined for UML 2.x. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::27]

feature.name: DAM_Profile
feature.description: A specialization of the MARTE profile for dependability analysis. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::30]

feature.name: Alloy_Language
feature.description: A fully declarative first-order logic language used to model complex systems and analyze security assertions. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::29]

and.name: Interoperability_Standards
and.description: Standards and specifications used to promote technical interoperability between different simulation systems and models, including security extensions and Linked Data approaches.

feature.name: SMP2_Standard
feature.description: Simulation Model Portability 2 standard proposed by ESA to promote model portability, reuse, and interoperability. Trace: [Article_10.pdf::chunk::31]

feature.name: HLA_Standard
feature.description: IEEE standard developed to promote interoperability between different simulation systems. Trace: [Article_10.pdf::chunk::1; Article_10.pdf::chunk::11]

feature.name: BOM_Standard
feature.description: Base Object Model specification used to propose interoperable and reusable model specifications. Trace: [Article_10.pdf::chunk::10]

feature.name: UMLsec
feature.description: An extension of the UML standard that provides a profile adding security properties in the form of stereotypes, tagged values, and application constraints. Trace: [Article_11.pdf::chunk::13]

feature.name: SecBPMN
feature.description: An extension of BPMN containing the SecBPMN-ml language which contributes security annotations related to properties like confidentiality or accountability. Trace: [Article_11.pdf::chunk::14]

feature.name: gRPC
feature.description: A communication protocol used for communication between the DesignSpace server and client-side extensions via proto requests and responses. Trace: [Article_5.pdf::chunk::141]

feature.name: OSLC_Standard
feature.description: Open Services for Lifecycle Collaboration standard adopting Linked Data and REST architecture for tool interoperability. Trace: [Article_6.pdf::chunk::1; Article_6.pdf::chunk::11]

feature.name: Sandbox
feature.description: A local copy of the Multi-Model Repository that allows modelers to work without being affected by concurrent changes. Trace: [Article_1.pdf §3.1 NAOMI Multi-model Repository]

and.name: System_Components
and.description: The software components that constitute the NAOMI platform architecture or support the federation infrastructure.

feature.name: Connectors
feature.description: Software components that connect individual models to the multi-model, isolating DSML specific interface code and enabling information exchange. Trace: [Article_1.pdf §3.3 NAOMI Components]

feature.name: Multi-Model_Manager
feature.description: The component responsible for integrating connectors, performing consistency checks, constraining attributes, and generating notifications. Trace: [Article_1.pdf §3.3 NAOMI Components]

feature.name: Execution_Automation_Engine
feature.description: The component responsible for determining execution order based on dependencies and orchestrating the execution process. Trace: [Article_1.pdf §3.3 NAOMI Components]

feature.name: Version_Control_System
feature.description: The system that keeps all artifacts under version control, enabling synchronization, rollback, and reconstruction of the multi-model. Trace: [Article_1.pdf §3.3 NAOMI Components]

feature.name: Middleware
feature.description: Software techniques or adapters used to link different simulation systems and models from different platforms. Trace: [Article_10.pdf::chunk::11]

feature.name: DesignSpace
feature.description: A versatile platform that facilitates the storage and reasoning of engineering knowledge in a multi-tool and multi-user environment, acting as a server for artifacts. Trace: [Article_5.pdf::chunk::131; Article_5.pdf::chunk::132]

feature.name: Plugin_Adapter
feature.description: Custom-built adapters responsible for translating between a tool's internal metamodel and the DesignSpace data representation, handling synchronization. Trace: [Article_5.pdf::chunk::139; Article_5.pdf::chunk::140]

and.name: OpenFlexo_Framework
and.description: A mature model-federation framework providing infrastructure to connect multiple models while keeping each in its technology space, including an FML engine and technology adapters.

and.name: Concept_Space
and.description: The location where models federation takes place, building on and enriching existing information to define new concepts and enforce consistency rules.

feature.name: FlexoConcept

and.name: F-IDE_Specification_Process

feature.name: Domain_Ownership

and.name: Intentional

feature.name: Simultaneous_Updates

feature.name: Scalability

feature.name: Technical_Interoperability

feature.name: Substantive_Interoperability

feature.name: Reusability

feature.name: Composability

feature.name: Security_by_Design

feature.name: Security_Oriented_Evolution

feature.name: Quality_Assessment

feature.name: Explicit_Knowledge_Representation

feature.name: Conceptual_Interoperability
feature.description: The objective of reconciling heterogeneous viewpoints expressed by stakeholders to ensure global consistency and understanding of the system. Trace: [Article_13.pdf::chunk::0; Article_13.pdf::chunk::2]

feature.name: Separation_of_Concerns

feature.name: Horizontal_Traceability

feature.name: Vertical_Traceability
feature.description: The ability to maintain traceability links for detailed analysis and refinement, connecting high-level requirements to detailed implementations. Trace: [Article_13.pdf::chunk::10; Article_13.pdf::chunk::27]

feature.name: Seamless_Integration
feature.description: The goal of achieving seamless and transparent integration of specialized representations and their tooling at low cost. Trace: [Article_13.pdf::chunk::23]

feature.name: Architecture_Understanding

feature.name: Project_Reuse

feature.name: View_Based_Consistency

feature.name: Viewpoint_Integration

feature.name: Explicit_Viewpoint_Relations

feature.name: Language_Reusability

feature.name: Explicit_Process_Modelling

feature.name: Multi_Tool_Consistency
feature.description: The goal of maintaining consistency across a myriad of tools and domains (e.g., mechanic, electronic, software) in collaborative development. Trace: [Article_5.pdf::chunk::1; Article_5.pdf::chunk::2]

feature.name: Fine_Grained_Synchronization
feature.description: The objective to synchronize artifacts at the level of model properties to ensure precise consistency across multi-domain engineering. Trace: [Article_5.pdf::chunk::13; Article_5.pdf::chunk::36]

feature.name: Avoid_Mega_Meta_Modelling

feature.name: Linked_Data_Semantics_Compliance

feature.name: Change_Traceability

feature.name: Impact_Assessment

feature.name: Semantic_Data_Exchange
feature.description: Ensuring the correct semantic precision of data exchange between models in the multi-model. Trace: [Article_7.pdf::chunk::13]

feature.name: Indirect_Relationship_Support

feature.name: Conceptual_Alignment

and.name: NFP_Integration

feature.name: Early_NFP_Detection

feature.name: Design_Space_Reduction

feature.name: Process_Automation_Goal
feature.description: The goal of automating error-prone steps of the software process to improve productivity and avoid late fixing of NFP problems. Trace: [Article_9.pdf::chunk::117]

feature.name: Multi_Paradigm_Modelling
